references.text: The parallel account in Matthew where the officer says he is not worthy for Jesus to come under his roof, with almost identical wording about humility before Jesus' authority.
Abraham shows hospitality to his heavenly guests but also expresses a humble attitude. Thematically parallel to the officer's humility before Jesus.
Peter falls at Jesus' knees and says, "Go away from me, Lord, for I am a sinful man." The same motif of unworthiness in meeting Jesus.
The prodigal son says, "I am no longer worthy to be called your son." The same motif of not considering oneself worthy, as the officer does here.
Jairus is told not to trouble the teacher any further. Here the officer asks Jesus not to trouble himself, a similar motif that Jesus need not be disturbed.
Peter tells Cornelius not to worship him, while Cornelius – another centurion – shows great humility. A parallel to the officer's humility in Luke 7.
The Canaanite woman shows great faith and humility before Jesus, similarly to the officer here, and Jesus commends her faith.
The Jewish elders go to Jesus on behalf of the officer and ask him to come. The context for why the officer then sends friends to say he is not worthy.
Jesus' response to the officer's humility and faith: he has not found such great faith even in Israel. Shows that the officer's declaration of unworthiness was actually an expression of great faith.
